name: Software team
description: A four-agent software team that works across your GitHub repositories: intake grills requests into specs, the architect designs, the implementer builds, reviews and QAs pull requests, and infra connects repositories, wires CI and deploys to Cloudflare. Work is tracked in a Supabase ledger; after human approval, harnesst merges.
setup:
Installing the team adds all four members to the team repository in one change and opens the setup wizard, which walks through everything the team needs in order: shared secrets (Cloudflare), the Supabase ledger (add a Supabase connection once in Settings → Connections and link it to the team; harnesst keeps it encrypted and applies future ledger migrations automatically), publishing, one GitHub App per member (created under your GitHub organization and installed on All repositories), approvals and agent wakes. Close it any time; the team's Setup link resumes where you left off.

GitHub access differs by role. Every member's App can read and write code, branches, pull requests and issues (labels, comments, closing). Only infra's App also gets Workflows, Actions secrets and variables, so infra alone can connect repositories to the ledger. No member's App gets Administration (it can edit branch protection and always bypasses its push allowlist), so a person creates each new repository under the organization and installs the team's Apps on it.

harnesst merges: after a person approves the merge gate, harnesst merges the issue PR at the approved head with its own GitHub App, which must be installed on every product repository. Agents never merge into the default branch. Recommended GitHub settings, applied by an org admin: an org ruleset on the default branch (require a pull request, block force pushes, restrict deletions, no bypass); per-repository branch protection with "Restrict who can push" allowing only your developers and harnesst's App, never the agents' Apps or GitHub Actions; and auto-merge disabled, since it would let a later agent commit land under a person's merge.

Once set up, talk to intake: "there's a bug in owner/repo: ..." or "build me a new app called ...".
